purpose: Can four small ChArUco patches at N/S/E/W find the plane of the animation disc in every rotation? First of a planned pair; the second will try NNE-NNW-SSE-SSW.
captured_note: Times are file mtimes, not shutter times; the frames were written directly rather than through bin/collect-captures, so no exposure was recorded per frame. 63 s for nine frames.

camera.name: v4k_01
camera.position: fixed throughout; not measured, recoverable from the poses

disc.facing_alignment_note: foam disc and black paper facing both cut to 16.5 in; they disagree by -2 to +5 mm at the extremes

paper.orientation: landscape, 279.4 mm E-W by 215.9 mm N-S
paper.artwork: printed hamster reference, not original art

protocol.intended_rotation_note: approximately 45 degrees CCW by hand; no objective measure
protocol.measured_rotation_note: recovered from the target poses; the sign is in the plane basis, whose handedness is arbitrary. Nine frames span 360 deg, so frame 9 repeats frame 1 to within 2 deg and there are eight distinct rotations.

lighting: hand-held cell phone, roughly above the disc centre
diffuse sunlight, sunny day, early afternoon -- moves during the session and is not reproducible

contamination.detail: A second printed ChArUco on the desk at bottom right emitted a valid marker id 5 in frames 1-3, colliding with piece #1 (E). RANSAC removed it; dropping those frames moves the answer by 0.084 deg, so the set stands. The stray has since been taken out of frame.

not_recorded: shutter times and per-frame exposure (no collect-captures manifest)
the camera's position and height, only its recovered poses
disc diameter, assumed 16.5 in rather than measured
how hard each target was pressed down, and its standoff
whether the paper shifted on its pegs between frames
